name: gforth
desc: Implementation of the ANS Forth language
why: A standards-following Forth with a stack-based mindset that rewires how you think about programs.

brief.what_it_is: Gforth is the GNU Project's implementation of the Forth language, a stack-based programming language. You run it as an interactive interpreter or batch-process Forth source files, and it compiles code to a fast direct or indirect threaded form using GCC. The homepage describes it as fully ANS/Forth 2012 compliant, with a large set of built-in words and libraries such as an object-oriented package written in plain ANS Forth. Input is Forth source or keystrokes at the prompt, and output is text on the terminal, files, or the program's own results.
brief.why_it_exists: The Gforth project's stated goal is to develop a standard model for ANSI Forth: to conform to the standard, to model its implementation-dependent parts, and to become widely accepted. The project also wants to be similar to earlier systems like fig-Forth and F83, powerful, efficient, free, and easy to port.
brief.how_it_works: The gforth binary is built on a virtual-machine generator called Vmgen, with primitives written in a small specification language and compiled through GCC into direct or indirect threaded code. Release notes describe two engines: gforth-fast, which is quicker, and gforth, the debugging engine that gives precise backtraces for signals such as illegal memory access but runs roughly 1 to 2 times slower. Dynamic and static superinstructions are used to speed up common sequences.

brief.install_notes: Brew installs several executables: gforth, gforth-fast, gforth-itc, gforthmi, vmgen, plus versioned copies named with -0.7.3. The source build needs GCC and runs install-deps.sh first. The 0.7.0 release notes say the runtime needs libtool and gcc (for the libcc C interface), and gdb for the SEE disassembler on some platforms. Debian and Ubuntu users can use a third-party net2o apt repo, and Docker or podman images exist. The homepage lists Windows, MacOS, and GNU/Linux as supported, plus the Gforth EC embedded variants for R8C, 4stack, MISC, and 8086.
brief.standout: Forth is a stack-based language with no conventional syntax, and Gforth is a full ANS-standard implementation with two execution engines, a debugger-friendly build, and a generator-based VM. Its embedded-control variants run on very small controllers such as 8086, R8C, and 4stack, which is unusual for a GNU project. The OO package being written in plain ANS Forth is also notable.
brief.status: Maintained, with some lag. The homepage names 0.7.3 as the current release, and its release notes run through 0.7.3. The GNU page was last modified 10 Nov 2015, which is old. gforth.org still has a Debian packaging guide that refers to Debian bullseye and later, a Docker image, and a live git repository on Savannah, so development is ongoing. The gforth.org page also mentions a tested version string of 0.7.9_20160714, which doesn't match the 0.7.3 release, so the exact version history is a little muddled.
brief.caveats: The runtime depends on libtool, GCC, and on some platforms gdb for the disassembler. Building from source requires a working GCC toolchain and install-deps.sh, which may need adjusting on less common systems. The 0.7.0 notes list changes that break older code, such as floored division and the rewritten TRY...ENDTRY. The Debian apt route depends on a third-party repository and a signing key. The homepage GNU page was last updated in 2015. I did not open the full user manual, so claims about the word set and the full standard conformance are the project's own statements.
